title: ÆTHER: The Oath (new track 6)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

positive_global_styles: an emotional, goosebump-raising sacrifice theme for a film: a lone bamboo flute rises to a huge choir, heartbreaking and proud at once, composed like a senior blockbuster film composer
the whole track walks in a 7-beat cycle (3+2+2, an Indian misra chapu tala), about 76 BPM, never plain 4/4: the limping pulse is the track's signature
a singable, slow flute melody in a minor raga (like Sivaranjani: a gentle sad flat third) with Carnatic gamakam slides and bends, built from question-and-answer phrases that develop and climb
the flute player's own breath is chopped into tight rhythmic glitch percussion: breath puffs, key clicks and finger taps on bamboo, stuttered and pitched, in the 7-beat cycle
a deep human heartbeat is the kick drum, a stretched low mridangam is the bass hit, a reversed veena swell rises into the main reveal

about half real instruments (bamboo flute, veena, mridangam, cello, violins, low brass, temple bell, a real choir) and half fresh, warm electronics (soft analog synth bass, granular shimmering textures, processed breath)
a wordless choir that grows from one hummed voice into a huge cinematic choir
clean, wide, warm, glossy mix with deep sub and a long airy reverb

positive_local_styles: the very first sound, at second zero: one deep temple bell strike with a low sub boom that rings out

then only ONE instrument: a lone bamboo flute plays a rising 3-note call (root, up a minor third, up to the fifth, the last note held and bent upward), very close and breathy, the flute's breath audible
a soft low drone enters under it at about 5 seconds, nothing else
transition: the flute's last note becomes a chopped, stuttered breath rhythm in the 7-beat cycle (3+2+2), like a limping heartbeat
a slow human heartbeat enters as the kick, the flute plays the main 5-note hook over the breath rhythm, one hummed female voice answers it
transition: the second temple bell strike, a cello takes the hook and the flute answers it with a counter-melody
soft analog synth bass moves like a second melody, mridangam joins the 7-beat cycle with the breath glitch percussion, warm granular shimmer around the flute
transition: a mridangam fill, then a proud slow march in the 7-beat cycle with big cinematic drums, low brass plays the hook, violins climb in counterpoint
a small choir of about ten voices hums the hook, growing
surprise: everything stops, only the heartbeat, slowing down: three beats, then two, then it stops completely
one full second of total silence, then the lone flute plays the hook, broken and slow, with the third temple bell

transition: a reversed veena swell rises into a massive slam: a huge full choir of a hundred voices sings the hook, the key lifts up a whole step, big drums, brass and strings in the 7-beat cycle at full power, the most goosebump moment of the track
the flute soars high above the choir with gamakam bends, the veena and the flute trade the hook phrase
the full band and choir hold one huge final chord with a deep sub drop, then fall away
only the lone flute is left: it plays the rising 3-note call once more, the last note held and bent upward, ringing into silence

brief.notes: Jithesh 29 Oct: an emotional sacrifice theme, a solo flute that rises to a full choir; he rejected Monsoon Duel as 'nothing unique', so uniqueness is the first job. What makes it ours: (1) the whole track walks in a 7-beat cycle (misra chapu, 3+2+2) instead of the usual 4/4, so the pulse limps like a heartbeat carrying a weight; (2) the flute's own breath is chopped into the rhythm (Broken Heritage: breath chiffs and key clicks as glitch percussion); (3) a heartbeat that is the kick drum and STOPS at the sacrifice; (4) a temple bell struck three times for the three vows; (5) the choir grows from one hummed voice to a hundred, never a choir pad from the start. Rules 9.1-9.14: one sound alone at first, layer by layer, a composed hook at every change every 8-12 s, about half real instruments, a key lift, a full silence and a slam, the motif at both ends.

story: A warrior swears an oath at a lamp-lit temple at night, knowing it will cost him his life. He keeps it, and a hundred voices carry his name after him.
